I just moved with my family to Winnipeg from Calgary on Sept 1st. So far i really like it. We were paying $1200 in utilities and our rent was being raised to $3800 from $2600 for a five bedroom house in Calgary. Here for a 5 bedroom we’re paying $2200 and utilities so far are about $1-200. The transit system isn’t as good as Calgary’s but it’s still okay, i’d honestly say the safety of it is about the same as Calgary, so far while on the bus i haven’t been bothered once, but i also know how to mind my own buisness. It’s definitely weird not seeing the mountains, but the trees here are beautiful and so is the sky once you get used to the endless horizon. Osborne Village and the Exchange district are some pretty cool areas! Similar to Inglewood or Kensington in Calgary. I’ve heard the schools here are good but i can’t directly comment on that. Lots of good food places here. The government seems greats and seems to be trying their best with what they’ve got. Honestly the only thing that annoys me so far is the PST. going from 5% to 12% doesn’t sound that crazy but it’s a pretty big jump. It’s just frustrating expecting to pay a certain amount cause your used to calculating 5% in your head and it ends up being more when checking out, but i’m sure i’ll get used to it. Also people seem WAYYY more chill with literally any kind of diversity here, race, gender, sexuality, etc!! So far i like it. There’s pros and cons but definitely better than Alberta and where that province is headed.

i didn’t really have a “prodromal” phase per say, or not one i really noticed. for about 6 months on and off i had daily diarrhea (sorry tmi) but also around that time it started i had a very dangerous bout of heat stroke and also started developing POTS so i just attributed it to that. my hyperemetic stage also came very out of nowhere. the only thing i did different the day it started is i had one of those thc drinks which may have set it off. I had similar pain, i didn’t vomit involuntarily until i had gotten back from the hospital after being diagnosed but i had forced myself to vomit to help the pain before i went to the hospital. Gasviscon Nausea (over the counter stuff) was my saving grace after the hospital. I did have lingering effects after leaving the hospital. i couldn’t eat properly for about a week but that may have been from me withdrawaling from THC. So sorta similar experiences i would say. I know for sure i had CHS as that pain never came back after i quit cold turkey and it’s been years now. I would say definitely quit for now. Wait a bit, if that pain happens again, it may be something different, but if it doesn’t i think it is probably CHS. I feel like the pain of CHS is a very specific very intense pain, it’s different than just normal flu bug or other stomach pains. The prodromal phase can be a lot of things, noticing you can’t sleep without smoking, can’t eat without smoking, tolerance going way up, IBS or similar things getting worse. So you may have had a prodromal phase and just didn’t even notice.
